digest.component_or_area: Reconciler baseline advancement and inbound field mirroring
propositions: The reconciler baseline is advanced from the pass-start snapshot before outbound mutations are applied, causing it to lag by one pass when the reconciler itself pushes a field value to Jira

A local status change (e.g. reopen) reverts silently when the new local value equals the stale baseline, because outbound suppression treats baseline equality as evidence that local is unchanged, allowing inbound to overwrite it

The defect is an ABA vulnerability: if local value X is pushed to Jira in pass N, the baseline remains at the pre-push value; if local reverts to the pre-push value before pass N+1, outbound suppresses the push and inbound clobbers with Jira's current value

The guard's premise (local == baseline implies local unchanged) is false for one pass after any outbound field mutation, affecting all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) which share the same _suppressed_by_inbound logic
Per-mutation success must gate baseline advancement to avoid recording a sync that did not occur when a soft-failing transition is caught by the backstop and the pass still exits 0

The fix restores ADR 0026's definition of baseline as last-synced (fetch overlaid with confirmed outbound pushes) rather than last-fetched, and closes test coverage gaps where direction-preservation cells existed only for title on an unused code path
